The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment to achieve parity with physical health, including counsellors in all schools. A National Cancer Control Plan and measures to end new HIV cases by 2030 are included.

## Social Care
The manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment for free personal care, increased carer pay with a career structure, and £3bn additional funding for children's social care. Disability benefits would increase by 5%.

## Housing
Plans include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
The manifesto targets wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences and fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be encouraged. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy
Proposed spending includes £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation. Railways, water companies, and major retail energy companies would return to public ownership. A wealth tax of 1-2% on assets above £10m would be introduced, alongside capital gains tax reform and alignment of investment income taxation with employment income rates.

## Employment
The manifesto proposes a £15/hour minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repeal of anti-union legislation, and a four-day working week. Gig economy workers would receive full employment rights.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, the five-week benefit wait would end, and the bedroom tax would be scrapped. Carer's allowance would increase by at least 10%.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would give legal personhood to nature. 30% of land and seas would be protected by 2030. Water companies would be nationalised. A new Right to Roam Act for England is proposed.

## Education
School funding would increase by £8bn, including £2.5bn annually for building repairs. Tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. SEND provision would receive £5bn investment.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Free bus travel for under-18s is proposed. New petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment, creating safe asylum routes, abolishing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and permitting asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy
The party supports an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident. Overseas aid would increase to 1% of GNI by 2033.

## Funding
Revenue measures include wealth taxes, carbon taxes, and business tax reforms estimated to raise £170bn+ by 2030. Additional borrowing would fund capital investment.

TEXT_B:
# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers arriving illegally. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences. A 20% National Insurance rate would apply to foreign workers (exempting healthcare workers and small businesses), with proceeds funding apprenticeships. Student visa rules would bar dependents, and a five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits.

## Economic Policy
**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 (removing 7 million people from income tax), cut stamp duty (0% below £750k), abolish inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and reduce fuel duty by 20p per litre while scrapping VAT on energy bills.

**Business:** Exempt businesses with profits under £100,000 from corporation tax, reduce the main rate to 15% by year three, raise the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolish business rates for high street SMEs, and introduce a 4% online delivery tax for large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed savings include stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion annually), requiring 5% efficiency savings across departments, halving foreign aid, and improving tax collection.

## NHS
Proposals include tax exemptions for frontline staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, removing student loan debt for medical staff serving 10 years in the NHS, and introducing patient vouchers for private treatment when NHS waiting time targets are missed. Weekend operating theatre use would be mandated.

## Energy
The party would scrap Net Zero targets and renewable energy subsidies, fast-track North Sea oil and gas licensing, grant shale gas test licences, and develop small modular nuclear reactors.

## Law and Order
Plans include recruiting 40,000 new police officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing with increased stop-and-search powers, building 10,000 new detention places, and introducing mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders.

## Education
Proposals include curriculum changes requiring balanced teaching of historical topics, banning gender transitioning discussions in schools, providing 20% tax relief on private school fees, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers.

## Benefits
The party would enforce a "two-strike rule" requiring benefit claimants to accept employment within four months or after two job offers, with face-to-face assessments for disability benefits.

## Defence
Spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with a pay review for armed forces personnel and a dedicated veterans ministry.

## Housing
Proposals include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping Section 24 tax rules for landlords, and abolishing the Renters' Reform Bill.

## Constitutional Changes
The party proposes leaving the ECHR, reforming the House of Lords, restricting postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation.

## Brexit
Plans include rescinding remaining EU regulations, abandoning the Windsor Framework, and renegotiating the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

## Funding
Total annual savings claimed: £150 billion (including £50 billion from departmental efficiency, £35 billion from QE reserve interest, £30 billion from scrapping Net Zero). Additional growth assumptions project £10 billion in extra tax revenue. Total annual costs: £141 billion.
